questions.q: Why do early layers of a model pretrained on a large, diverse dataset tend to transfer well to a new task?
options: They are randomly re-initialized before transfer
They typically learn general-purpose patterns like edges and textures, useful across many different image tasks
They contain the classifier head, which always matches the new task exactly
They are the only layers that use convolutions
questions.explain: Early layers of a network trained on a large, diverse dataset tend to learn general visual features (edges, textures, simple shapes) that are broadly useful, not specific to the original task.

Loads a ResNet-18 architecture with the best available pretrained weights for that model
Trains a ResNet-18 from scratch on the current dataset
Deletes the model's final classifier layer automatically
questions.explain: Passing weights=ResNet18_Weights.DEFAULT loads the architecture with the recommended pretrained weights for it, using torchvision's current weights-enum API.

questions.q: After setting `param.requires_grad = False` on every parameter of a pretrained model and then replacing `model.fc` with a new `nn.Linear` layer, which parameters actually get updated during training?
options: No parameters are updated anywhere in the model
Only the new nn.Linear layer's parameters, since newly created parameters default to requires_grad=True
Every parameter in the model, including the frozen backbone
Only the first convolutional layer
questions.explain: Freezing existing parameters sets their requires_grad to False, so backpropagation skips them. The newly created nn.Linear layer defaults to requires_grad=True, so it's the only part of the model that trains.

questions.q: What is the key difference between feature extraction and fine-tuning in transfer learning?
options: Feature extraction trains the entire model from random weights; fine-tuning only trains the new head
Feature extraction freezes the whole pretrained backbone and trains only a new head; fine-tuning unfreezes some or all of the backbone to adapt it further
They are two names for exactly the same technique
Fine-tuning can only be used with convolutional layers, never with linear layers
questions.explain: Feature extraction keeps the pretrained backbone frozen and trains only the new head. Fine-tuning goes further by unfreezing some or all of the backbone (typically at a lower learning rate) to adapt it to the new task.

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend using `weights.transforms()` when preparing input images for a pretrained model?
options: It is purely optional and has no effect on model accuracy
It applies the exact resize/crop/normalize pipeline the pretrained weights were trained with, and mismatched preprocessing can quietly hurt accuracy
It freezes the model's backbone automatically
It replaces the need for a DataLoader entirely
questions.explain: Each pretrained weights object specifies the exact preprocessing (resizing, cropping, normalization) it was trained with. Using a different pipeline can silently degrade accuracy without causing an error.
